clue.text: Starts to deliver unusually brief service for dead author

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words give their opening letters only
a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A priest rattles through an unusually short service in memory of a dead writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes D and U; 'brief' trims MASS to MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas, the French novelist, died in 1870, so he is a late writer.

clue.text: Old boat struck yacht, out of control after chain's slipped

indicators.note: letters out of control are thrown into a new order
something that has slipped has fallen away, so these letters are lost from the fodder

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for chain, the old unit of length

explanation.surface: A runaway yacht hits an old vessel after its anchor chain gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipped' removes C and H from STRUCKYACHT, leaving STRUKYAT, which 'out of control' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is a famous nineteenth-century tea clipper preserved at Greenwich, a historic sailing ship.

clue.text: Tight cord flexed when first pulled

parts.note: string is a thin cord

indicators.note: the first letter is pulled away from the word

parts.note: flexed means bent

explanation.surface: A cord goes taut when flexed and given a first tug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first pulled' removes B from BENT to leave ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are tight or strict, a close synonym.

clue.text: Where kiwis are given old label attached with ring

parts.note: a tag is a label
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Somewhere New Zealanders are given an old label fixed on with a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwis are New Zealanders, not just the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island, home to many people nicknamed kiwis.

clue.text: Set to catch little round bird

indicators.note: one word catches the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to set one against another is to pit them

indicators.note: turned round means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A trap is set to catch a small round bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like the verb to place, but here it means to pit one against another; 'round' and 'to catch' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, or lapwing, is a plover named for its call.

clue.text: Keep isn't commonly guarded by chief

indicators.note: something guarded by another sits within it

parts.note: main means chief, principal
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A castle keep is said to be guarded by its chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going is to maintain it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: President that is backing opponents at table in disreputable group

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are reversed
one piece is placed in another

parts.note: a shower is British slang for a useless or disreputable bunch
at the bridge table East and North are opposing partners, giving E and N

explanation.surface: A president backs a team of card-table opponents mixed up with a dodgy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit North, South, East and West, with North-South against East-West. 'Shower' is British slang for a useless lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States.

clue.text: Outstanding head of social services — the best

parts.note: an ace performer is outstanding

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An outstanding head of social services is hailed as the best.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis an ace is a service the receiver cannot touch, so aces are the best serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are unreturnable serves in tennis, the finest a player can deliver.

clue.text: Run and see bank

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone runs off to check out a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the usual crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on them, so bank as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Swore, angry about high kicks

indicators.note: about here means turned around, signalling a rearrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Someone cursed angrily about a high kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'about' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a garryowen is a high up-and-under kick, named after a Limerick club.

clue.text: Hike rearwards then forwards

parts.note: back means to the rear
in rugby the forwards are known as the pack

explanation.surface: A walker goes back and forth along a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forwards' is a rugby term: the forward players make up the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to hike with your gear carried on your back.

clue.text: Nap of snooker baize that's been cut off-centre

indicators.note: the phrase has its centre cut away, leaving only the outer parts

explanation.surface: Someone dozes on a snooker table whose cloth has been trimmed unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off-centre' removes the middle KERBAI from SNOOKERBAIZE, leaving SNOO and ZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooze is a short sleep, the same as a nap.

clue.text: About to quit new cinema film genre

indicators.note: something made new is reshaped, so its letters are rearranged
a letter that quits leaves the word it was in

parts.note: c., short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Somewhere close to giving up on a new cinema showing a certain film style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to quit' takes C from CINEMA, and 'new' rearranges INEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animated film, a genre of cinema.

clue.text: Organ given by short tough girl

indicators.note: short means cut off before its last letter

parts.note: hard means tough
Monica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tough young woman supplies a church instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims HARD to HAR; 'given by' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ.

clue.text: Do not begin to tease and attack scapegoat

indicators.note: the word does not begin, losing its opening letter

parts.note: to taunt is to tease
a sally is a sudden attack or sortie

explanation.surface: Advice to stop teasing and attacking someone who carries the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do not begin' drops the T of TAUNT. An Aunt Sally is a British fairground target, figuratively one who takes undeserved criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a fairground target, hence a person set up for attack or blame.

clue.text: Gorgeous girl in US city taking speed?

parts.note: NY is short for New York
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A beautiful young woman in New York is she on drugs?
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a beautiful young woman, from the nature spirits of myth.

clue.text: One fool given power to stop favourite walk

indicators.note: to stop something up is to plug it, so these letters fill the gap inside

parts.note: a dear is a favourite person
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sap is a fool
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A fool given power stops a favourite's walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' puts ISAPP inside DEAR. 'walk' here means vanish, as stolen goods walk.
explanation.definitionFit: When things walk they go missing, the slang sense of vanishing into thin air.

clue.text: Oberon perhaps left stranded in lake

indicators.note: something stranded in a place is stuck inside it

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: The fairy king of Shakespeare's play is left stranded in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon suggests the fairy king, but it is the actress Merle Oberon.
explanation.definitionFit: Merle Oberon was a film star, so Oberon is a surname belonging to someone called that.

clue.text: Conscious male is avoiding mawkish emotion

indicators.note: a word avoiding a letter leaves it out

parts.note: sentiment is soppy emotion

explanation.surface: A conscious man avoids over-sentimental feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is avoiding' drops M from SENTIMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being is aware and able to feel, effectively awake to the world.

clue.text: Clubs fashion champ

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
to hew is to shape or fashion with cuts

explanation.surface: Golf clubs make the latest fashion for a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like champion but is the verb to munch.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or bite noisily, much as to masticate.

clue.text: Pyramids built of earth rated fantastic

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly unreal, here signalling the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Pyramids built of earth are considered fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built of' just links; 'fantastic' rearranges EARTHRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a triangular pyramid; tetrahedra is the plural.

clue.text: Girl against wearing that nightie — extremely

indicators.note: a piece wearing another has it on, enclosing it

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
V stands for versus, against

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl objects to wearing a nightie that is too extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts V inside YON; 'extremely' takes N and E from nightie.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvonne is a female first name.

clue.text: Come down heavily on a hanging for smuggling heroin

indicators.note: a hanging used for smuggling carries something hidden inside it

parts.note: a valance is a short drapery hanging from a bed frame or pelmet
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone gets clobbered for hanging around smuggling heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links; 'for smuggling' puts H inside VALANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To avalanche is to fall in a great heavy mass, as snow does down a slope.

clue.text: Famous king and knight wrapping present

indicators.note: letters wrapping others enclose them

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
now means the present time

explanation.surface: A celebrated king and knight wrap a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it means the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well known is famous, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pop might be so dejected with everything about cold interjection

parts.note: low means dejected

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: all means everything
oho is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Dad may be down and shouting about the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is fizzy drink, not father. 'about' puts COHO inside ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy soft drinks are generally free of booze or have only a little.

clue.text: Second vote choice

parts.note: an election is a vote

explanation.surface: A second vote gives voters a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is what is picked, a choice.

clue.text: In Scotland, English school accepting a head initially appointed from the south

indicators.note: something accepting another takes it inside
in a down clue reading from the south means bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a ness is a headland

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter

explanation.surface: In Scotland a school takes on an English head appointed from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from the south' reads upwards, applied to the headland word. A ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours on Scottish coasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is the Scots term, often scornful, for an Englishman.

clue.text: Wife visiting an abbey in Central Park?

indicators.note: one who is visiting is in a place, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: Downton Abbey is the fictional house of the television drama

explanation.surface: A wife visits an abbey in New York's Central Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Downton Abbey is a British TV period drama. The definition is loose: a park in the centre of a city is downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtown is the central district of a city, where a central park would be found.

clue.text: Meal's starter fully dropping stimulants

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped completely

parts.note: suppers are evening meals

explanation.surface: A meal's first course is dropped in favour of pep pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course, but it is the opening letter of SUPPER'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppers is slang for amphetamines and other stimulant drugs.

clue.text: Excellent woman's lingerie, very alluring up front

parts.note: a bra is lingerie

indicators.note: up front means at the start, the first letter

explanation.surface: A woman's underwear is very alluring at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVA is the cheer of praise given to a female performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brava is the feminine form of bravo, applauding a woman's fine performance.

clue.text: Number 10 beginning to upset MP following reshuffle

indicators.note: after a reshuffle the letters sit in a new order

parts.note: 10 looks like the letters I and O

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter

explanation.surface: Downing Street starts to upset an MP after a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 is the Prime Minister's residence, but 'Number' means something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic that dulls pain, so it is a numb-er.

clue.text: Host taking off trolley after bishop's gone

indicators.note: a letter that has gone is removed from the word

parts.note: off one's trolley means crazy, barmy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A host carries off a trolley after the bishop has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'taking' link. 'Off one's trolley' is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number of people, especially an army.
